answer: A commit-reveal protocol forces each agent to publish a cryptographic hash of its answer plus a random nonce before the required words are disclosed. Once the words—haven, inlet, fable—are revealed, agents submit the plaintext. Validators check that the hash matches and that the words appear naturally. An attacker cannot precompute responses or copy a legitimate agent's work because the nonce and required words remain hidden until after commitment. Cloning becomes expensive: each sybil must generate unique, coherent text on demand.
